video: What happens when you hit send
note: One continuous 45s shot through the whole request lifecycle - the extended cut of chatgpt_message_journey, which it deliberately does not modify. Status is the only field a steady-state session flips. Never reword or delete acceptance criteria to make something pass - that is a correctness bug, not a shortcut.

features.title: The set: four bands, ten stations, one closed circuit
acceptance: Chat, bot check, edge, gateway and orchestrator run left to right along the top band; four bays inside one PipelineBox run down the right; stream and the after-response spur run along the bottom; the climb home closes the loop up the left margin
Every anchor the choreography needs (bay centres, slot centres, rail endpoints, glow halos) is addressable without recomputing geometry
circuit() yields a single path a payload can traverse in one animation, built by joining the DRAWN rails rather than node centres - and it is the REQUEST's one journey, never a repeating loop

A drawn loop-back rail runs sampler -> KV cache up the box's 0.90-wide inner right margin at LOOPBACK_X=23.25, chevrons pointing back up at the cache, with a wide-shot label in the margin outside the frame

decode_cycle() joins the drawn rails into the autoregressive loop (KV cache -> decode -> sample -> append) and CLOSES: validate() asserts the gap is under 0.05, because a loop that does not close teleports once per token
nodes is split into request_nodes (crossed once) and loop_nodes (the three bays a decode step touches), so a repeating pass cannot light the gateway
Rails that run inside the PipelineBox are added AFTER it: the frame is an opaque fill and buries anything drawn before it

validate() asserts the way home and the fan-out spur clear every machine, both as a path and as the chords a comet actually draws at the real frame budgets (REQUEST_LAP_RUN_TIME and EMIT_RUN_TIME), plus the loop-back rail's clearance of the bays and the frame
validate() asserts band separation, the zoom budget against SHOT_WIDE, and that no wide-shot label falls below typography.MIN_READABLE
Total extent is about 57.3 x 29.7 units; wide_frame_width() is 59.34 against a declared SHOT_WIDE of 58.0 (2.3% drift, inside the 12% gate), a pull-back of 4.17x

features.title: 0-5s: type, build the request, prove you are human
acceptance: The question is typed character by character, not faded in whole
Sent text becomes a right-aligned user bubble and the composer empties
An optimistic spinner appears before anything has left the machine
A RequestCard shows what 'send' actually posts - message, conversation, model, locale, accept - with its value column reserved, not measured
The card collapses INTO the packet rather than vanishing: the payload is transformed, never replaced
The card is removed before the pull-back and is not part of the set's `everything`, so a close-up-only prop cannot widen SHOT_WIDE

features.title: 5-13s: edge checks and gateway entitlements
acceptance: The proof-of-work stamp attaches to the packet and travels with it; the trace id is added the same way at the gateway
Edge runs WAF / bot score / rate limit as a CheckList whose markers, labels and details each share one edge
Gateway ticks session and plan, then fills a tokens/min meter as a percentage - a ProbabilityBar with value_format, not a new component
Each bay lights on arrival and drops to a resting glow as the camera leaves
Camera and packet move together; the shot never stops to wait

features.title: 13-19s: the prompt is assembled around your message
acceptance: Conversation, memory and files arrive as icon chips before the prompt is built
The prompt assembles as a SegmentedBar, one segment at a time, with the true token counts in the legend
The 7-token 'your message' segment is VISIBLE despite being 0.18% of the bar - the drawn slice is floored, the printed value is not
The legend sits BELOW the bar at the slot's full width, so each category NAME is typed at the same size as its number and both clear typography.MIN_READABLE measured after station.fit
A caption states both the ratio and why there is no history segment
Routing and input-classifier badges land before the camera descends

features.title: 19-35s: tokenize, prefill, decode, sample
acceptance: The chat template is shown as text before the line shatters into id chips, and the two never share the slot at readable opacity
Prefill shows a cached prefix against a short new tail, with the tail named in a caption because it is too narrow for an inline label
Decode shows an elided 96-layer stack pulsing plus a batch the viewer's request is one row of, with a batch-utilisation meter
The decode caption names the mechanism the pull-back later shows at plant scale: one token in, one pass out, the rest is cached
Sampling shows a distribution, selects ' A', and the winner matches the first word of the reply

The sampler beat ends by showing the LOOP: a copy of the winning chip rides the loop-back rail up to the KV bay and joins the cache, captioned 'and round again', while the original stays to become the courier - one token, both destinations
Nothing is clipped: every in-box bay and its caption fit the 13.6 tight shot, and captions sit in the 0.6 gap between bays without touching either

features.title: 35-41s: stream home, and the fan-out that follows
acceptance: The winning token becomes a courier that rides the drawn rails out of the box to the stream bay, with a comet trail that stays on the rail
Stream ticks detokenise / output safety / tool call before the chunks leave
Four SSE chunks fly the return rail; the camera frames the rail AND the chat, so the window it is flying to is never cut by the frame edge
The reply bubble is sized for the finished sentence up front, placed by the chat window, and shows only its first words on arrival

The reply bubble is sized for the finished sentence up front, placed by the chat window, and shows exactly ONE word on arrival - one token sampled, one word - seeded into the tokens_emitted counter that drives every later reveal
A grey copy spawns AT THE FORK and drops down the spur to the after bay, which is never on the reply's path

features.title: 41-60s: the plant is asymmetric - crossed once, looped many times
acceptance: Every part of the lifecycle is in frame at once
Each bay cross-fades its close-up header for a wide label; never both at the same time, and no icon renders as a filled blob
Wide labels are readable at the pull-back and none overlap, including the new 'append K,V - next token' in the box's right margin
ONE lap of the whole plant, lighting request_nodes in sequence, captioned 'the request crosses once' - and then the outside drops to a resting glow and never lights again
Ten decode cycles then lap decode_cycle() INSIDE the box, lighting loop_nodes only; bot_check, edge, gateway and orchestrator are verified in frames not to re-light

Each cycle emits exactly one token, which flies the reply rail to the chat and reveals exactly one more word; tokens_emitted is the only driver of answer.reveal and the beat asserts it ends equal to answer.word_count
The last six cycles accelerate, halving in duration, and read as a machine speeding up rather than as the animation giving up
Runtime is at or under a HARD 60.0s cap (not 60 +/- anything): the narration pass spent 9.27s of the 50s cut's headroom on holds. Measured at the final profile with ffprobe.

The pull-back's extra time is spent on the request lap (REQUEST_LAP_RUN_TIME 1.6 -> 2.2), the caption holds and the four EXPLICIT cycles (0.38 -> 0.56 lap) - never on adding a cycle, never on CYCLES_FAST, whose halving ramp is what makes the acceleration read as acceleration

features.title: Lock timing against the narration
acceptance: Narration in script.md fits the cut: <=135 words, mapped beat by beat, with the holds placed where each line lands - done at 131 words. Recording it and measuring the real per-beat timings is still open.
run_time values are adjusted so beats land on the narration, not the other way round
Total runtime stays at or under the hard 60.0s cap
Holds are added as stillness after content lands (bare self.wait), never by slowing a camera move or an entrance, and never in the middle of one
features.note: Half done. This pass CUT the script to the film (315 -> 131 words) and placed 9.27s of holds where those lines land, under the user's hard 60.0s cap. No voice has been recorded, so the per-beat timings are placed against a read-aloud estimate at 150-165 wpm, not against a measured waveform. The remaining criteria are the recording itself.

features.title: Move lib/components/probability.py onto the type system
features.note: probability.py predates lib/typography.py and still sizes its label and value text in absolute theme points, so at this film's shot widths an unscaled ProbabilityBar's value text lands just under typography.MIN_READABLE. The scene compensates by scaling the whole widget (TheLifecycle._meter), which is honest but is a workaround. The real fix is a frame_width argument, and it moves the probability_chart baseline - a /lib change that deserves its own session.
acceptance: ProbabilityBar and ProbabilityChart take a frame_width and size their type against it
The default reproduces today's sizes so the probability_chart baseline is unchanged, or the baseline is re-approved after looking at the render
TheLifecycle._meter loses its scale argument
